expected.reason: Coverage is strong, but pre-tax income fell 27%, all $1.45B of debt matures in 2028 inside the loan term, and a change of control was pending. The change of control is a flag on its own.

discussion: Claude's read, confirmed by Joel 2026-10-09. Mismatch. The model is wrong, not the expectation. Tranche PASSes at 84 because it cannot see the two things that drive Joel's FLAG: all $1.45B of debt maturing in FY2028, inside the loan term (AUDIT P1-21), and the pending change of control (AUDIT P1-22). The earnings point is weaker than it looked: pre-tax income fell 27%, but EBITDA was flat ($665M in 2023, $663M in 2024, from the prior-year columns of R4 and R7). The drop came from depreciation and interest. | Update 2026-10-09, Claude's read, Joel to confirm: With cash taxes, rent and working capital added, Tranche now FLAGs (match), but not for Joel's reasons. The flag comes from main's combined severe cash-flow stress (cash-flow DSCR 0.43x), which holds maintenance capex at the $423M depreciation estimate while revenue falls 20%. A rental company would cut fleet spend in a downturn, so this is the conservative end. Right verdict, different reason: P1-21 and P1-22 are still needed for Tranche to see what Joel saw.

maintenanceCapex.estimate: Depreciation ($423.3M, mostly rental fleet) used as maintenance capex proxy. Actual 2024 purchases were $344.6M rental plus $106.6M other.

caveats: TIMING: last 10-K before the 2025 Herc acquisition. Screen is as of February 2025.
ASSUMPTION, rating: H&E's February 2025 rating could not be verified. Weak is a conservative assumption. Adequate would lower the spread by 200 bps, from +200 to 0.
JUDGMENT, working capital: the $42.3M fall in accounts payable likely includes rental fleet purchase timing. Working capital absorbed $36.9M; without the payables line it released $5.5M.
